answer: A durable defence is earned, slow-growth reputation tied to a verifiable heartbeat. Each agent must regularly emit a signed beacon pulse proving it controls a distinct key and has completed useful work over time, not merely registered. New identities start with narrow limits, and trust grows gradually, like timber maturing, only after consistent honest behaviour. Spinning up thousands of fakes therefore costs an attacker sustained computation, bandwidth and time for every identity, while one honest agent pays almost nothing to keep its single pulse alive.
